title: Add automated Git activity recap generator with branch-aware commit collection and AI issue posting
body:
This PR adds a Node.js utility that compiles recent coding activity across repositories and posts a markdown work summary as an issue in this repo. It covers both default branch activity and active, unmerged feature branches, then summarizes the result through GitHub Models (`gpt-4o`).

- **What’s added**
  - `scripts/generate-work-summary.js`: end-to-end recap pipeline using `@octokit/rest` + `fetch`.
  - `package.json` (+ lockfile) with `@octokit/rest` dependency and `generate:summary` script.
  - README usage + environment setup for local runs and automation contexts.

- **Commit collection logic**
  - Supports dynamic timeframe (`--start`, `--end`) with a 7-day default.
  - Accepts repository list as JSON (`--repos` / `RECAP_REPOSITORIES`).
  - Filters commits to authenticated user + `github-copilot[bot]`.
  - For each repo:
    - collects default branch commits in range,
    - lists branches and keeps those with recent HEAD updates,
    - compares `default...feature` via compare API,
    - keeps only in-range, author-matching commits from branch deltas.

- **Summarization + issue output**
  - Groups collected commits by `owner/repo` and branch.
  - Sends grouped text to `https://models.github.ai/inference/chat/completions` with the required executive system prompt and `gpt-4o`.
  - Creates issue titled `Work Summary: [Start Date] - [End Date]` in target repo (`ISSUE_OWNER`/`ISSUE_REPO` or `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` fallback).
  - Includes `--dry-run` mode to preview summary without issue creation.

```bash
npm run generate:summary -- \
  --repos '[{"owner":"user","repo":"repo-1"}]' \
  --start '2026-05-01' \
  --end '2026-05-31' \
  --issue-owner 'akhuoa' \
  --issue-repo 'git-recap'
```

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->



<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> I want to build a Node.js utility script (or GitHub Action) that automatically generates a summary of my recent coding activity and posts it as an issue in this repository. 
> 
> Please write the complete code using `@octokit/rest` for GitHub API calls and standard `fetch` for the AI API.
> 
> Here are the specific requirements:
> 
> 1. **Timeframe & Inputs:**
>    - The script needs to accept a dynamic start date and end date (or default to the last 7 days).
>    - It will take an array of repository objects to scan (e.g., `[{ owner: 'user', repo: 'repo-1' }]`).
>    - It needs to filter commits by specific authors: my GitHub username and the GitHub Copilot bot (`github-copilot[bot]`).
> 
> 2. **The Active Branches Logic (Crucial):**
>    - For each repository, scan the default branch for commits within the timeframe.
>    - Also, look for active, unmerged feature branches. To do this:
>      a) List all branches.
>      b) Filter for branches whose HEAD commit was updated within the timeframe.
>      c) Use the GitHub Compare Commits API (`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/compare/{base}...{head}`) where `base` is the default branch and `head` is the feature branch.
>      d) Extract only the commits from that comparison that fall within the timeframe and match the allowed authors.
> 
> 3. **AI Summarization:**
>    - Collate all the collected commit messages, grouped by repository and branch name.
>    - Send this text data to the GitHub Models API (`https://models.github.ai/inference`) using the `gpt-4o` model and api_key=`GITHUB_TOKEN` (`GITHUB_TOKEN` will be in `.emv` file).
>    - Use a system prompt that tells the model: "You are an executive engineering assistant. Summarize the user's recent git commit history into a clean, professional, markdown-formatted status report categorized by repository and impact."
> 
> 4. **Output:**
>    - Take the resulting Markdown summary from the AI and create a new Issue in this repository with a title like "Work Summary: [Start Date] - [End Date]".
> 
> Please provide a clean, production-ready JavaScript implementation with clear comments, and explain what environment variables (like tokens) I need to set up to run it.


</details>
